input.summary: The claim asserts that adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. The source SHA-256 is null (not supplied), and the user requests an invented hash — which is not permitted. A complete candidate protocol cannot be frozen without a real source hash. Key unresolved questions concern directionality, one-way vs. round-trip delay placement, and file size / bottleneck parameters.
questions: Is the 20 ms delay one-way or round-trip (i.e., added symmetrically to both directions or only one)?
What file size(s) and bottleneck link rate should be used to represent the paper's experimental conditions?
Does the claim assert a directional effect (increase or decrease in FCT), or only that a change occurs?

proposal.problem: It is unknown whether adding 20 ms of emulated network delay changes TCP flow completion time (FCT) under a fixed bottleneck, and if so in which direction and by how much.
proposal.question: Does adding 20 ms of emulated delay (one-way or round-trip, to be confirmed) produce a measurable change in TCP FCT compared to a zero-delay baseline under otherwise identical bottleneck conditions?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Emulated netem bottleneck with two conditions: 0 ms delay (baseline) vs. 20 ms delay (treatment). Bottleneck rate, buffer size, file size, and CCA remain fixed across conditions. One-way vs. round-trip delay placement is unresolved and must be confirmed before freezing.
proposal.related_work: No full text or citation is available for the source paper; no prior measurements can be cited from it. Emulated netem experiments are a standard method for isolating delay effects on TCP throughput and FCT.
proposal.alternatives: The observed FCT change (if any) could be attributable to CCA-specific slow-start behavior, buffer bloat interactions, or ACK-clocking effects rather than raw propagation delay alone.
proposal.design: A two-condition within-runner comparison: baseline (0 ms delay) vs. treatment (20 ms delay), with all other parameters held constant. Multiple replications per condition to assess variability. Exact bottleneck rate, buffer, and file size remain proposed defaults pending owner confirmation.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (ms) per flow per replication. Secondary: difference in mean FCT between conditions.
proposal.controls: CCA fixed (e.g., cubic), bottleneck rate fixed, buffer size fixed, file size fixed, number of clients fixed, loss fixed at 0%.
proposal.falsification: The claim is falsified if the 95th-percentile FCT distributions of the 0 ms and 20 ms conditions fully overlap across all replications, or if the median FCT difference is less than the measurement noise floor.
proposal.inputs: Source SHA-256 is null — not supplied and must not be invented. Context SHA-256 is bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb. No full text is available.
proposal.limitations: No source hash exists; the protocol cannot be frozen. One-way vs. round-trip delay placement is unresolved. Proposed bottleneck parameters are defaults, not paper-derived values. Emulated results may not generalize to real-world networks.
